passiveDetection.title: Passive Detection (traps, clues, secret doors)
passiveDetection.hint: Draw a Region where something hidden really is, add the 'Passive Detection' behavior to set its skill, DC, range and the message the player gets. Whenever a PC comes within range, their passive score against the DC decides whether they notice it. Once per PC per spot. Secret doors are configured on the wall itself instead.

hiddenCreatures.title: Hidden Creatures (passive Perception)
hiddenCreatures.hint: Mark an NPC's token as both hidden on the canvas and carrying the Hiding status, and every PC that comes within range is checked: their passive Perception against the creature's passive Stealth. Nothing is revealed - the player is told privately that they have noticed something. Once per PC until the creature hides again.

lockpicking.title: Lockpicking
lockpicking.hint: Clicking a locked door as GM offers to attempt picking it with the currently controlled/selected PC's Thieves' Tools instead of the default silent 'locked' behavior. The lock's DC is set once per door and remembered.
lockpicking.noActor: No controlled/selected token to attempt the lockpick with.
lockpicking.setDcHint: This door's lock difficulty hasn't been set yet. Set it once - it will be remembered for future attempts.
lockpicking.success: {name} picks the lock successfully. The door is now unlocked.

monsterRecognition.title: Monster Recognition (passive knowledge)
monsterRecognition.hint: When combat starts, every PC is checked against every hostile monster present: the correct passive knowledge skill for that creature type against DC 10+CR. Whoever meets it gets the monster's name and description in chat. Once a PC has recognized a kind of monster, later encounters always recognize it, with a compact message. Configure descriptions and skills from the 'Monster List' panel in Settings.

screenAlert.name: On-screen alert as well as chat
screenAlert.hint: When a PC notices something, also pop a brief notification on the owning player's screen. The whisper in chat is sent either way - this only adds a nudge, since a chat line is easy to miss mid-scene.

secretDoorDefaultDC.name: Secret doors: default DC
secretDoorDefaultDC.hint: Used by every secret door that has no DC of its own, so a freshly drawn one already works.

secretDoorDefaultRange.name: Secret doors: default range
secretDoorDefaultRange.hint: Distance in scene units within which a PC's passive Perception is checked against a secret door.

creatureDetectionRange.name: Hidden creatures: detection range
creatureDetectionRange.hint: Distance in scene units within which a PC's passive Perception is compared with a hidden creature's passive Stealth. Without a limit, a high passive would notice an ambush across the whole map.

wallConfig.hint: Only applies to walls whose door type is Secret. Leave a field empty to use the world default shown as its placeholder.

secretDoor.spotted: {name} spots something odd about this stretch of wall (passive Perception meets/beats DC {dc}).
secretDoor.notSpotted: {name} passes a secret door without noticing it (DC {dc}).

dc.label: Detection DC
dc.hint: The passive score (for whichever skill is chosen above) a PC needs to meet or beat to notice this.

range.label: Detection Range
range.hint: Distance (in scene units) from this Region's footprint within which a nearby PC triggers the check.

skill.label: Passive Skill
skill.hint: Which passive the PC is checked on. Perception for something noticed in passing, Investigation for something that has to be pieced together.

message.label: Message on Success
message.hint: What the player is told when their PC notices this, e.g. 'One flagstone sits a finger lower than the others'. Leave empty for the generic line. Never shown on a failure.

requiresSight.label: Requires Line of Sight
requiresSight.hint: If set, a wall between the PC and this spot prevents detection. Turn off for something noticed by sound or smell around a corner.

passiveDetection.spotted: {name} notices something suspicious nearby (passive check meets/beats DC {dc}).
passiveDetection.notSpotted: {name} passes close to something hidden without noticing it (DC {dc}).
passiveDetection.migrated: Passive Detection: {count} trap behavior(s) converted to the new format.
passiveDetection.migrationFailed: Passive Detection: {count} behavior(s) failed to convert, will retry next load.
passiveDetection.migrationError: Passive Detection: migration failed unexpectedly, see console for details.

hiddenCreatures.spotted: {name} catches movement that should not be there (passive Perception meets/beats DC {dc}).
hiddenCreatures.notSpotted: {name} walks past something hidden and lying in wait (DC {dc}).

markerWarning.needsHidden: {name} is marked as Hiding but its token is still visible to players, so it will not be detected. Hide the token too.
markerWarning.needsStatus: {name} is hidden from players but has no Hiding status, so it will not be detected. Add the status if it is meant to be lying in wait.

surprise.title: Surprised by the Ambush?
surprise.hint: These PCs did not notice at least one hidden creature on this scene. Uncheck anyone who should not be surprised, then confirm. Apply this before rolling initiative - dnd5e grants the disadvantage at roll time.

monsterRecognition.noDescription: The character recognizes the type of creature, but no description has been set by the GM.
monsterRecognition.recognizedByActive: {name} recognizes it after an active {skill} check (DC {dc}).
monsterRecognition.missedPassive: {name} fails to identify {monster}: passive {skill} below DC {dc}.
monsterRecognition.missedActive: {name} attempts a {skill} check to identify {monster}, but falls short (DC {dc}).
monsterRecognition.unresolvedSkill: Monster Recognition: could not determine the knowledge skill for '{name}' (no type set). Fix it from the Monster List panel.

activeCheck.noActor: No controlled/selected PC to attempt the knowledge check with.

list.title: Monster List
list.menuHint: View and correct the match, knowledge skill and description of every NPC in the world for Monster Recognition.
list.hint: A monster is auto-matched to an internal database entry when its name matches. Use 'Edit' to link a different one or write a custom description.
list.name: Name

editDialog.title: Edit Recognition — {name}
editDialog.descriptionHint: Replaces the linked monster's description. Leave empty to use the linked one above, if any.

aboleth.description: Ancient aquatic horror that enslaves minds with a single touch and never forgets a grudge.

beholder.description: Floating orb covered in eyes, each capable of a different magical ray, paranoid and obsessed with its own uniqueness.

mind-flayer.description: Tentacle-headed humanoid that feeds on brains and bends other minds to its will, servant of a psionic order from elsewhere.

wolf.description: Pack hunter able to bring down much larger prey by isolating it from the herd.

dire-wolf.description: Huge, vicious wolf that hunts in organized packs, often at the command of something that can control it.

giant-spider.description: Horse-sized spider that spins rope-strong webs and injects a paralyzing venom.

giant-rat.description: Oversized rodent that lives in large colonies in sewers and dungeons, often carrying disease.

brown-bear.description: Large territorial predator, slow to charge but lethal once at close range.

pegasus.description: Winged horse of celestial nature, proud and loyal to those who prove pure of heart.

deva.description: Golden-winged celestial messenger, sent to guide or protect at crucial moments.

animated-armor.description: Empty suit of armor animated by magic, with no will of its own beyond the last order it was given.

flesh-golem.description: Construct stitched from corpse parts and woken by lightning, brutal and prone to uncontrollable rage.

stone-golem.description: Colossus of carved stone, slow but nearly indestructible, made to guard a place for centuries.

red-dragon.description: Chromatic dragon tied to fire and greed, the most vain and territorial of its kind.

black-dragon.description: Chromatic dragon of swamps and stagnant water, corrodes what it touches with acid and shows no mercy to trespassers.

blue-dragon.description: Chromatic dragon of the deserts, proud and tactical, hurls lightning and loves ambushing from the sand.

green-dragon.description: Chromatic dragon and manipulator who enjoys intrigue and poisoned favors as much as its toxic breath.

white-dragon.description: The most primitive and brutal chromatic dragon, dwelling in glaciers and frozen caves.

fire-elemental.description: Living pillar of flame that sets alight everything it touches, feeling no pain.

water-elemental.description: Sentient mass of water that can engulf and drag under anyone it grabs.

air-elemental.description: Living whirlwind, fast and elusive, as hard to hit as it is to outrun.

earth-elemental.description: Animated mass of rock and soil, slow but able to move through solid stone.

pixie.description: Small fey that can turn invisible at will, fond of pranks and subtle magic.

dryad.description: Spirit bound to a single tree, protector of the forest who can charm intruders.

satyr.description: Goat-like fey, fond of music and pleasure, as festive as it is unpredictable.

imp.description: Small shapeshifting devil often kept as a spy or familiar, slippery and untrustworthy.

quasit.description: Small, cowardly, servile demon that can turn into animals to spy unnoticed.

vrock.description: Screeching vulture-demon that sows chaos in battle with cries that weaken the mind.

hell-hound.description: Red-furred infernal hound that hunts in packs and breathes fire.

succubus-incubus.description: Seductive demon/devil that feeds on the life force of those it seduces, a master of deception.

ogre.description: Brutish, dim-witted giant-kin armed with a club, driven more by hunger than strategy.

troll.description: Regenerating predator that heals from nearly any wound unless burned or dissolved with acid.

hill-giant.description: The crudest and most voracious of giants, driven only by hunger and brute strength.

frost-giant.description: Warrior giant of frozen lands, proud of its strength in battle.

fire-giant.description: Giant smith and strategist, disciplined and organized into near-military forces.

goblin.description: Small, cunning, cowardly humanoid that lives in large warrens and acts in groups, quick to flee when things turn bad.

hobgoblin.description: Militaristic, disciplined humanoid that organizes its kin into well-coordinated tactical units.

bugbear.description: Hairy, surprisingly stealthy humanoid despite its bulk, fond of ambushes and sneak attacks.

orc.description: Warrior humanoid that lives for battle and conquest, often organized into tribal warbands.

kobold.description: Small reptilian humanoid that makes up for its weakness with clever traps and group tactics.

gnoll.description: Hyena-like humanoid driven by an insatiable demonic hunger that makes it ruthless in battle.

bandit.description: Common outlaw, often part of a gang, that lives off robbing travelers on the road.

drow.description: Elf of the deep underworld, skilled in magic and blade, raised in a ruthless, hierarchical society.

owlbear.description: Unnatural cross between an owl and a bear, fierce and territorial, attacking anything that nears its nest.

manticore.description: Beast with a lion's body, bat-like wings and a scorpion tail that hurls venomous spikes.

chimera.description: Hybrid creature with the heads of a lion, a goat and a dragon, each attacking in its own way.

medusa.description: Snake-haired humanoid whose gaze turns anyone who meets it to stone.

minotaur.description: Bull-headed guardian of labyrinths, ferocious and nearly impossible to lose once it has your scent.

mimic.description: Shapeshifting predator that disguises itself as a common object, often a chest, to lure unsuspecting victims.

gelatinous-cube.description: Transparent gelatinous mass that slides through dungeon corridors, dissolving everything it traps.

ochre-jelly.description: Acidic ooze that splits in two whenever struck by a slashing weapon.

black-pudding.description: Corrosive ooze able to dissolve metal and wood, splitting when struck by slashing or bludgeoning damage.

shambling-mound.description: Animated heap of rotting vegetation that feeds by absorbing the organic matter of its victims.

treant.description: Ancient tree awakened to consciousness, a slow but devastating protector of the forest.

skeleton.description: Bones reanimated by necromantic magic, with no will of its own beyond following orders.

zombie.description: Slow, rotting reanimated corpse, nearly immune to pain and surprisingly hard to put down for good.

ghoul.description: Ravenous undead that feeds on human flesh, its claw paralyzing anyone not immune.

wight.description: Intelligent undead that drains life force with its touch and can raise zombies from its victims.

wraith.description: Incorporeal spirit wrapped in a dark cloak, draining life with a chilling touch and nearly immaterial.

vampire.description: Aristocratic, seductive undead, immortal as long as its home coffin remains intact, feeding on blood.

lich.description: Spellcaster who gave up life for immortality, its spirit anchored to a phylactery hidden elsewhere.
